input: This capital appraisal examines the case for a solar array with an installed cost of $1968k and an expected net saving of $478k per year sustained over a period of 12 years. Discounting the anticipated savings at a discount rate of 10% produces a present value of the savings of $3257k, and once the installed cost has been deducted, the resulting net present value stands at $1289k. On a purely undiscounted basis, the cumulative savings would pass the installed cost at some point during the fifth year of operation, with the discounted surplus being accumulated over the remainder of the array's service life. It is important to note, however, that the entire case rests on the savings, and the savings in question are vendor and utility estimates; no saving has as yet been measured on a comparable installation, which means that the income side of the appraisal remains unmeasured across the whole of the period it purports to cover. The estimation risk is located principally in two places, namely the electrical output of the array itself and the price of the electricity that the output displaces, and any shortfall in either of these will erode the saving year after year, causing the net present value of $1289k to fall correspondingly, with no offsetting item available on the cost side once the installation has been completed. The positive figure should therefore be interpreted as a surplus that materialises only if the savings arrive broadly as estimated, rather than as a measured or guaranteed return on the investment.
target: The solar array has a net present value of $1289k at a discount rate of 10%, and the appraisal supports installation on the estimates as given. Installed cost is $1968k. The expected net saving is $478k per year for 12 years. Discounting the savings at the stated rate gives a present value of $3257k, and the net present value is the present value less the installed cost: $1289k. On an undiscounted count, the savings pass the installed cost during the fifth year of operation, and the discounted surplus is earned over the rest of the array's life. The case rests on the savings, and the savings are vendor and utility estimates. No saving has yet been measured on a comparable installation, so the income line of the appraisal is unmeasured for the whole period it covers. The estimate risk sits in two places: the output of the array, and the price of the electricity the output displaces. A shortfall in either one reduces the saving year by year, and the net present value falls with it, with no offsetting item on the cost side once the array is installed. The appraisal also takes the savings as level across the period, which is the estimators' own presentation of them. The figure is positive, and it is positive on estimates. The decision should be taken with the figure read that way: a surplus over the discount rate if the savings arrive as estimated, not a measured return.
